interest: Index of 1938–39 reporting on Japanese militarization, bureaucratic rivalries and cabinet changes, with views from other capitals.
overview: This file comprises thirteen docket sheets ('List of Papers', sheets 67 through 79) from the U.S. Department of State's central decimal file 894.00 (Political Affairs - Japan), recording documents received and dispatched between March 1938 and December 1939 (sub-numbers 732 through 885). The register chronicles critical internal political developments, cabinet reorganizations, and administrative shifts in Japan amidst the escalating Second Sino-Japanese War. Major subjects documented include the successive cabinets of Prince Fumimaro Konoe, Baron Kiichirō Hiranuma, and General Nobuyuki Abe; factional struggles within the government over military prosecution versus diplomatic settlement of the China conflict; the controversial establishment of the Asia Development Board (Kōa-in) and related colonial development companies; state economic control and spiritual mobilization under the National General Mobilization Law; diplomatic disputes with the United States and Great Britain regarding the Open Door, foreign rights, and property damage in China; and Japan's diplomatic maneuvering regarding the Anti-Comintern Pact, European alliances, and the outbreak of World War II.

subfiles.about: A thirteen-page Department of State purport list indexing and summarizing incoming and outgoing communications, memoranda, and cross-references regarding Japanese internal political affairs from March 1938 through December 1939.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: This register systematically catalogs diplomatic despatches, telegrams, memoranda, and cross-references concerning internal Japanese politics between March 1938 and December 1939 (document sub-numbers 732 to 885). Key topics indexed include the successive reorganizations of the Konoe, Hiranuma, and Abe cabinets, internal government debates over prosecuting the war in China versus seeking a negotiated peace, and the controversial creation of the Asia Development Board (Kōa-in) and trade control organs. The entries summarize reports submitted by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, Embassy Tokyo staff, and consular officers across East Asia and Europe concerning spiritual and economic mobilization under the National General Mobilization Law, the protection of American property rights in China, and diplomatic friction surrounding the Anti-Comintern Pact. The sheets also record internal State Department distributions, cross-references to other decimal files (notably 793.94 and 894.002), and departmental commendations of embassy reporting officers.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Political Affairs - Japan (File 894.00, Sheets 67–79, Sub-numbers 732–885)
